# Allowlist for .github/scripts/secret_scan.sh. Read that script's header for the format.
#
# PUBLIC IPv4 LITERALS ARE FORBIDDEN in every tracked text file, PR title/body and
# commit message, except the ranges below. This file lists what is safe to publish;
# it never names a host of the estate, and nothing about the estate's own servers
# belongs here. A new entry needs a reviewer who can say why the address is public
# by design.
#
# Reserved / non-routable ranges: safe by definition.
ipv4 0.0.0.0                # unspecified address
ipv4 10.0.0.0/8             # RFC 1918 private
ipv4 127.0.0.0/8            # loopback
ipv4 169.254.0.0/16         # link-local
ipv4 172.16.0.0/12          # RFC 1918 private
ipv4 192.168.0.0/16         # RFC 1918 private
ipv4 224.0.0.0/4            # multicast
ipv4 240.0.0.0/4            # reserved (class E)
ipv4 255.255.255.255        # limited broadcast
# Documentation ranges (RFC 5737): the right addresses for examples.
ipv4 192.0.2.0/24           # TEST-NET-1
ipv4 198.51.100.0/24        # TEST-NET-2
ipv4 203.0.113.0/24         # TEST-NET-3

# Public-looking addresses already in the repository, none of them an estate host.
# Each is scoped to the files that carry it, so the same address anywhere else is still a finding.
ipv4 213.186.33.5 docs/AI_HANDOVER.md docs/PRODUCTION_RUNBOOK.md   # former shared-hosting DNS target, documented as such
ipv4 1.2.3.4 reference/api.js tests/ida-v12-vehicle-identification-test.js   # dummy client address in a comment and a log-redaction fixture

# Fixture that must look like a credential to prove the log redactor strips it.
skip credential-literal tests/ida-v12-vehicle-identification-test.js
